problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=2x+3{y}^{2}$ on the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2}.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Average Value of a Multivariable Function

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function
examples.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y) = xy$ on the region $D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: -1 \leq x \leq 2, \: x \leq y \leq 3x \big\}$ given that the area of the region is $3$ square units.
examples.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{x}^{3x}xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-1}^{2}[\frac{x{y}^{2}}{2}]_{y=x}^{y=3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-1}^{2}4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[{x}^{4}]_{x=-1}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(16-1) \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)$ and the region $D$ given by

$$
f(x,y)=6{x}^{2}-2y+2,\,D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1}.
$$

According to the mean value theorem for double integrals, there exists a point $(a,b)\in D$ such that the volume of the solid enclosed between the surface $z=f(x,y)$ and the $xy$-plane over the region $D$ equals the volume of the right cylinder with base $D$ and height $f(a,b).$ Find $b$ given that $a=\frac{1}{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
According to the mean value theorem for double integrals, there exists a point $(a,b)\in D$ such that

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A=f(a,b)\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

Evaluating the integral on the left-hand side, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}(6{x}^{2}-2y+2)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(6{x}^{2}-2y+2)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[6{x}^{2}y-{y}^{2}+2y]_{y=0}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(6{x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =[2{x}^{3}+x]_{x=-1}^{x=1} \\  & =(2\cdot {1}^{3}+1)-(2\cdot (-1)^{3}+(-1)) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=1\cdot 2=2.
$$

Also, we are told that $a=\frac{1}{2}.$ So, our initial equation simplifies to

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =f(\frac{1}{2},b)\cdot 2 \\ 6 & =(6\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}-2b+2)\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =\frac{7}{2}-2b \\ -\frac{1}{2} & =-2b \\ b & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{4})\in D.$ Therefore, the answer is $b=\frac{1}{4}.$
